About the role:

You'll build and run the AI voice agents that talk to Salmon customers every day, taking them from collections into telesales and possibly customer service.

What you'll do:

 - Ship voice agents that call real customers, and see their effect on collections and sales numbers within weeks.

 - Work across the voice stack: telephony, speech recognition, text-to-speech, LLMs, and the backend services that connect them.

 - Join a small voice platform team and work directly with the Head of AI/ML, who leads it. You own real problems, and your ideas shape what we build next.

What you'll own:

 - Build new voice agents for collections, telesales, and other use cases, from conversation design and prompts to production rollout.

 - Tune the voice itself: choose and configure TTS voices, fix how agents pronounce Filipino names, amounts, and dates, and adjust pacing and turn-taking so calls sound natural.

 - Evaluate new ASR, TTS, and LLM models against our current setup on accuracy, latency, cost, and Tagalog and Taglish quality, then integrate the ones that perform better.

 - Maintain evaluation sets and test-call routines, so every change to an agent is measured before release.

 - Monitor live agents on call quality, latency, cost per call, and conversion, and fix the issues you find in recordings and transcripts.

 - Ship production code through Git, merge requests, code review, tests, and CI/CD, and document your agents, experiments, and decisions.

What makes you a strong fit:

 - Fluent Tagalog and English. You can tell when a bot sounds unnatural to a Filipino customer and explain why.

 - 1 to 3 years of commercial software development, ideally in Python.

 - Working knowledge of Git and branching, merge requests and code review, automated tests, CI/CD, separate environments, and logging.

 - Backend basics: REST APIs, JSON, async calls, and reading a vendor's API documentation to connect a new model.

 - Practical experience with LLMs and AI agents: pet projects, coursework, or shipped features. Engineers moving into AI from data engineering, data science, or backend development are welcome.

 - Clear written English: you document what you build and explain trade-offs to the team.
